newsitem.title: MEXICO: NAFTA panel says U.S. dumps flat steel in Mexico. [CORRECTED 20:12 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NAFTA panel says U.S. dumps flat steel in Mexico. [CORRECTED 20:12 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and text to say panel ruled the United States was dumping flat recovered steel)

A U.S.-Mexican binational panel established under the North American Free Trade Agreement has upheld a Mexican anti-dumping measure against U.S. flat recovered steel imports, the Mexican Trade Ministry (Secofi) said on Friday.

But the panel ruled that Mexico's calculations on the damage done to local steel producers were incorrect and its standards on what constitutes dumping and its anti-dumping tariffs are too high, according to a Secofi spokeswoman.

In a statement published in the official gazette on Friday, Secofi said the panel decided on September 23 Mexico had the right to impose an anti-dumping tariff on U.S. flat recovered steel before it finished its dumping investigations.
"The panel ruled dumping exists and upheld Mexico's right to impose the tariffs, but it decided Mexico's dumping calculations were incorrect," said the spokeswoman, who wished to remain anonymous.

The panel, made up of three Mexican and two U.S. representatives, was investigating an August 1994 Secofi resolution that imposed a 38.2 percent tariff on U.S. exporters with the exception of LTV Steel and Bethlehem Steel Corp, Secofi said. -- Mexico City newsroom, +525 728-9565
